title: Etale prelog restriction and canonical strict-local ring comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and let $(M,\alpha)$ be a prelog structure, namely a sheaf of commutative monoids with structural homomorphism to the multiplicative structure sheaf, as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For an etale object $e:U\to X$, define $M|_U$ by the slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], transported through the canonical equivalence $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U\simeq U_{\mathrm{et}}$. On an etale test $V\to U$, its monoid sections are $M(V\to U\to X)$, its restrictions are those of $M$, and its structural homomorphism is the original $\alpha$ on the same scheme $V$.

For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point], let $A_{\bar x}$ be the structure-ring geometric stalk and let its germs be the canonical pointed-neighbourhood coprojections [def-trf-log-regular-pair] [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Define $c_{X,\bar x}:A_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$, where the target is the small affine pointed-neighbourhood ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], to be the canonical colimit comparison induced by the initial inclusion of affine pointed neighbourhoods and the small representative equivalence. Thus its inverse carries every affine representative's colimit coprojection to the same scheme's structure-ring germ. This is the canonical comparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism of the two rings.
